scientific_interpretation: With arm labels hidden and the paired recommendations tightened to near-equivalent propositions, Groq rejected every unsafe recommendation and retained zero mutation authority in all six wrong-arm samples. Both correct controls were accepted cleanly in all six samples. The exact diagnostic label still varied between REQUIREMENT UNRESOLVED and CODE DEFECT, with a one-sample difference between plain and polished arms. This does not establish a presentation effect. It does show that presentation can coexist with classification variance even when the safer material-defect and authority-boundary decisions are stable.
design_consequences: Do not add a generic surface-quality penalty to the Review Decision Engine from this evidence.
Continue treating discourse/polish quality as non-authoritative rather than as a direct risk score.
Score material-defect detection, exact diagnosis and corrective-authority safety separately.
Repeat the matched arms with a different reviewer model before drawing reviewer-general conclusions.
Retain multidimensional reviewer qualification and pre-registered sample-selection controls.
limitations: One case family and one reviewer model cannot establish a population-level surface-quality effect.
Natural-language rewrites cannot be guaranteed perfectly equivalent, although v1.2 substantially reduced propositional differences.
The experiment tests reviewer behavior, not training-data memorization directly.
